Definition: from G50; a thing ignored, i.e. shortcoming:--error.
BiblicalUsage: Agnoema is an error — a thing done in ignorance, a shortcoming — and it appears once, in the description of the Day of Atonement: the high priest entered the second part of the tabernacle once a year, 'not without blood, which he offered for himself, and for the errors of the people.' The word covers the sins the people did not even know they had committed, and the blood covered those too.
TheologicalSignificance: The high priest carried blood for his own errors as well as the people's, and this word names the errors — the verse holds the mercy, not the noun.
